summary: Host only; nothing flashed or run. canary-trig-fault (canary-trig + BRK #0x1234 after the first report round, -DMK_FAULT_ROUND=0) builds reproducibly (two builds identical): Image f839ba305fae5e89c48642b422a827bc4993d491681560b2b20fd1a46b560a1b (49152 B), packaged with the NAT-006 builder into RECOVERY image e7ab288fdd689dcb15c58cf92e19a96586b30ec3b85a6df09695d3b41772a735 (19608 differing 4 KiB pages, canary at offset 2048). canary-plain 7bc1b01d, canary-fault 38a4feba, canary-trig 572ebd0f and loader-diag dc46bdec are byte-identical to build-002. 21 host tests pass (python3 -m unittest docs/procedures/nat-022/test_nat022.py), including the exception loop with kicks against the fake DECON0: marker before any MMIO, only TRIG_CON/SHD_REG_UP_REQ written, ESR/ELR/FAR/slot read back by the independent decoder, no MMIO when a kick was interrupted or the MMU is on. make check passed (214 tests; it does not include test_nat022.py). Not shown by any host test: the AArch64 vector entry (exc_common), the BRK itself and the EL2 ESR/ELR reads (no AArch64 emulator here); the 19 s BRK timing rests on two observations of the display ending ~60 s after the first marker, not on a measured timeout. session_trigfault.py refuses to run unless docs/decisions/0011-nat022-canary-trig-fault-single-run-2026-11-10.md exists; that decision is not made. The image-specific request is in the README section 'canary-trig-fault' and is put to the owner in the session.
